subject: Stage-gate: evaluation plan + hosting/region preference (Hosted -> Dedicated fallback)
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@clearpathhealth.com>

Cc: Tom Chang <tom@clearpathhealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-09 09:12 -0700
Subject: Re: evaluation kickoff & residency constraints

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran the legal/infosec review and two points came up that will shape our evaluation plan: EU data residency for patient identifiers, and a clear timeline for a go/no-go decision tied to procurement.

Can you share a stage-gate style MAP that lays out: 1) short POC (hosted) to validate latency and quality, 2) a dedicated EU environment option if we need stronger isolation, and 3) the path to a private on-prem deployment if required for the regulated workflows? Ideally that MAP has concrete acceptance criteria and deadlines we can take to procurement.

We also need a list of SOC2 and data-retention artifacts (summary is fine) for the security questionnaire.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m call if helpful.

Samantha Lee
Head of Data Integrations
ClearPath Health

Attachment: CPH_eval_questions.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@clearpathhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09 11:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stage-gate: evaluation plan + hosting/region preference (Hosted -> Dedicated fallback)

Hi Samantha —

Thanks — attached is a draft MAP (CPH-MAP-v1.xlsx) and a short SOC2 evidence summary. High-level proposal below, focused on minimizing time to value while preserving an escape hatch to Dedicated/Private if regulatory gating requires it.

Stage 0 — Kickoff (week 0)
- Confirm scope: inference for patient triage summaries, sample dataset (anonymized) delivered by 5/12.
- Logistics: sign MSA addendum for evaluation (data processing addendum included).

Stage 1 — Hosted POC (2 weeks: 5/13–5/26)
- Objective: validate latency (<300ms median for 512 tokens), throughput (100 qps burst), and quality on our prompt set.
- Acceptance criteria: 90% of prompts meet quality thresholds in eval set; latency SLO met; no critical security gaps from questionnaire.
- Deliverables: test harness results, token-cost estimate, SOC2-summary and audit checklist.

Stage 2 — Dedicated EU pilot (optional, 3 weeks: 5/27–6/16)
- Trigger: if POC shows data residency/regulatory issues or procurement demands dedicated capacity.
- Objective: deploy to dedicated GPU pool in eu-west region with private networking; verify performance parity and isolation controls (VPC peering, KMS integration).
- Acceptance criteria: audit evidence for data residency, identical eval quality, cost/runbook for cutover.

Stage 3 — Private (on-prem/VPC) (timeline TBC)
- Trigger: explicit regulatory requirement or enterprise procurement mandate.
- Objective: plan for customer-managed deployment; produce deployment runbook, support SLA, and gap analysis.

Closing & procurement timeline
- Preferred go/no-go checkpoint: 6/18 — procurement needs decision (hosted continue vs. commit to Dedicated contract).
- Desired production pilot start: 7/01 if Dedicated chosen, otherwise continue on Hosted with committed SLA.

Questions for you:
1) Is the 2-week Hosted POC window workable for your engineering team?
2) Do you want the Dedicated EU pilot to be an automatic follow-up if procurement flags residency, or should we wait for the POC outcome?

I'll tag Karthik and Jonas for technical inputs (batching, KV cache behavior, and estimated cost deltas).

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
Mobile: (555) 618-4420

Attachments: CPH-MAP-v1.xlsx, SOC2_evidence_summary.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-10 08:22 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stage-gate: evaluation plan + hosting/region preference (Hosted -> Dedicated fallback)

Priya / team —

Quick technical notes to support the MAP:
- Hosted POC is the fastest path. For the latency target (~300ms median for 512 tokens) we recommend using a Redwood-verified 8-bit quantized model variant and enabling prefix caching for repeated prompt fragments — that should keep cost low while meeting SLOs.
- Dedicated EU pilot: we can spin a dedicated pool in eu-west within 48–72 hours after contract signature if capacity is available. Dedicated gives stronger isolation (no multi-tenant kernels) and simplifies audit evidence (separate tenancy logs).
- Private/on-prem: largest lift — estimate 8–12 engineer-weeks for initial deployment runbook plus networking/KMS integration; needs a separate pricing/managed-support proposal.

Cost deltas (very rough): Hosted POC incremental cost for 2 weeks ~ $6k–$12k depending on QPS and model size. Dedicated EU pilot (3 weeks) runway ~ $18k–$30k (includes reservation + usage). Private build-phase is a one-time eng effort + monthly platform fee; we'll scope after you confirm interest.

I'll prepare a short tech appendix (batching settings, recommended quant profiles, KV-cache hints) and attach it to the MAP by EOD.

— Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment stub: tech-appendix-stagegate.pdf

If all good I'll ask procurement to reserve budget for the Dedicated fallback but hold off on signing until after 6/18.
